solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disoriented American being judged away from public gaze

definitions.text: being judged away from public gaze

indicators.note: someone disoriented has lost their bearings, so the letters lose their order and are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, all eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A confused visitor from the States is tried behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disoriented American' reads as a description of a person, but it is the anagram signal plus its fodder; IN CAMERA is Latin for 'in the chamber'.
explanation.definitionFit: A case heard in private, with press and public excluded from the courtroom, is said to be heard in camera.

clue.text: Worthless bunch or individual engaged in demonstrating?

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for a useless, contemptible group of people
second meaning: one who shows, read as SHOW plus the agent ending -ER

explanation.surface: A useless crowd, or a lone protester at a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'what a shower!' dismisses a hopeless lot; the second sense is the playful 'one who shows', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shower is British colloquial scorn for an inept group, and literally anyone who shows or exhibits something.

clue.text: Sequence of events arranged in a score

indicators.note: to arrange music is to rework it, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, all eight letters

explanation.surface: A run of happenings set down as music in a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' and 'score' make the clue sound musical, but the eight letters of 'in a score' are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an imagined or planned outline of how a series of happenings could unfold.

clue.text: Hardly fair

blocks.note: first meaning: barely, by a narrow margin
second meaning: equitable, morally right

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'Hardly fair' sounds like a complaint about unfairness; split, the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb meaning barely and as an adjective meaning equitable or righteous.

clue.text: You are reportedly holding certain person taking a lot of interest

definitions.text: person taking a lot of interest

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the words are taken by their spoken sound
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: the word is said like the letter U, as in text-speak
certain means sure
the word is said like the letter R, as in text-speak

explanation.surface: Someone apparently keeps hold of a person who is very interested in things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You are' in text-speak becomes U R, and SURE sits between the two letters; 'taking a lot of interest' sounds like curiosity but means charging high interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant rates, so they literally take a great deal of interest on loans.

clue.text: Was familiar with Kafka’s first novel

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the word it follows

blocks.note: the initial letter of the writer's name
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: Someone knew the debut book by Franz Kafka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, continuing the Kafka picture, but it is the adjective meaning fresh or original.
explanation.definitionFit: To have known something is to have been acquainted or conversant with it, the past tense of know.

clue.text: Cautiously move part of hand or foot

blocks.note: first meaning: to edge forward slowly and carefully
second meaning: a unit of length, a fraction of both the hand and the foot measures

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand or foot' suggests a finger or toe, but both are units of length: a hand is four of the answer, a foot twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to creep along gradually, and an inch is a small imperial unit making up hands and feet.

clue.text: Running right into relative — good

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a cousin is a family relative
R is the standard abbreviation for right
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Racing straight into a family member, which turned out fine.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside COUSIN, and G is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Coursing describes liquid or blood flowing rapidly, the way water courses or runs down a channel.

clue.text: State of Asia — it’s holding area back, washed-out

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece goes inside another
going back means turning around, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the pronoun taken as written, the apostrophe-s linking it to what it holds
A is the abbreviation for area
wan means pale or washed-out

explanation.surface: An Asian nation, it seems, keeps a faded region at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washed-out' sounds like a description of the state, but it is just a synonym for pale; the apostrophe-s in 'it's' is the surface's glue, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is the island nation off the Chinese coast in East Asia, a self-governing country.

clue.text: Cast in support of sitting ruler, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase asks us to judge by what we hear rather than by spelling

blocks.note: a monarch sits supported by a ceremonial chair, which is said the same as the past participle of throw

explanation.surface: Something is cast to prop up a monarch on the seat of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a verb meaning to make in a mould or choose actors; it is the past participle of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast and thrown are both past participles of verbs for hurling or flinging something away.

clue.text: Fruit skin, we hear – or two

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words are taken by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: to pare is to peel or skin
two of a kind make a pair

explanation.surface: Peeling a fruit, or a couple of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Two different spoken words, one meaning peel and one meaning a couple, both sound exactly like the answer, so either route works.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet tree fruit with a rounded base narrowing towards the stalk.

clue.text: Wrongly parse her word, in other words

indicators.note: something done wrongly is out of proper order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, all eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone misreads her sentence and has to explain it differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word' is a verb here, to express in words; adding 'in other words' gives the verb for expressing again differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To rephrase is to express the same idea again using different language or phrasing.

clue.text: Naval ship in which to be dressed overall?

definitions.text: in which to be dressed overall

blocks.note: first meaning: HMS of that name, the vessel in the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera

blocks.clueFragment: in which to be dressed overall
blocks.note: second meaning: a sleeveless garment worn over clothes, an overall

explanation.surface: A warship decked out with flags from stem to stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed overall' is the naval term for a ship hung with flags, which fits 'naval ship'; here it means wearing an overall. HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron-like garment worn over clothing, and it names the fictional ship of the famous operetta.

clue.text: Cushy job at home acquired by firm

indicators.note: what is acquired is taken in, so one piece ends up inside another

blocks.note: firm means secure, fixed fast
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A company takes on someone for an easy post they can do from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company doing the acquiring, but it is an adjective meaning stable; IN goes after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position demanding little or no actual work, the classic easy number.

clue.text: Dispirited team of players with county

blocks.note: the cast is the company of actors in a production
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A dejected sports side that represents a county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team of players' suggests sport, but these players are actors. Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cast down is an idiom for feeling dejected, depressed or low in spirits.

clue.text: Reasoning without conclusion, however

indicators.note: lacking a conclusion means lacking an ending, so the final letter is removed

blocks.note: reasoning is thought, the process of thinking

explanation.surface: An argument that never reaches its conclusion, however.
explanation.walkthrough: THOUGHT loses its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are concessive connectives that introduce a qualification, as in 'it was cold, though sunny'.

clue.text: Apply colour that’s fashionable time after time

indicators.note: after says what comes later, setting the order in which the pieces join

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
what is in fashion is in
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone keeps choosing paint in whatever shade is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' sounds like 'repeatedly', but it supplies T twice; IN plus T comes after the other T.
explanation.definitionFit: To tint is to give something a slight shade or hue, colouring it lightly.

clue.text: Coverage for building (not this church)

blocks.note: the alternative to this is that
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Insurance cover for a building, but not this particular church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' suggests insurance, but it is a roof covering; the bracket reads as an aside yet supplies both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reeds laid over a roof, a covering for a house or cottage.

clue.text: Every year, install a deity inside temple

indicators.note: to install something is to put it in place within, so one piece goes inside another
inside places the following words within the surrounding letters

blocks.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year
taken as written
a deity is a god

explanation.surface: Every year, a god's statue is set up within a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: PA, short for per annum, surrounds A plus GOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple across East Asia.

clue.text: Centre of Kalahari Desert is this

definitions.text: Centre of Kalahari Desert is this

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so the letters come from within the run of words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the join between the two words

explanation.surface: The heart of the southern African desert is very dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the end of 'Kalahari' and the start of 'Desert', and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of a great desert is parched and dry, receiving almost no rainfall.

clue.text: Tip of cross covered by primate

indicators.note: in a down answer, something covered by another lies beneath it, fixing the order

blocks.note: an ape is a primate
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A monkey has hidden the end of a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the covering word sits on top, so APE comes above X.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or peak of something, its very top.

clue.text: Catastrophe, as foci changed

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, all six letters

explanation.surface: Disaster strikes when the points of attention shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foci' is the plural of focus, chosen because its letters fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure or complete disaster, a debacle.

clue.text: Tragedy of family meeting regal oddball

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric and out of line, so the letters are thrown out of order
two things meeting come together side by side, so the pieces join

blocks.note: your kin are your family
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A family gathering with an eccentric royal ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddball' looks like a noun for an eccentric person, but it is the signal to rearrange REGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is one of Shakespeare's great tragedies, about an old monarch and his daughters.

clue.text: Fish or beef

blocks.note: first meaning: a freshwater fish
second meaning: as a verb, to complain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish or beef' sounds like a menu choice; 'beef' is the slang verb meaning to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A carp is a freshwater fish, and to carp is to find fault or complain persistently.
